races.name: Sligo Plumb Centre Mares Maiden Hurdle

runners_data.name: Belladaball
runners_data.note: Gavin Cromwell's five-year-old owns the class ceiling here at OR 120 with a win on Good ground in her profile, but she is a genuine hold-up operator running in a race where the rear is crowded — she will need a clear run from midfield and a strong jump at the last to bridge the gap to Cotswold Blue.|

runners_data.name: Cotswold Blue
runners_data.note: Sole front-runner from Mullins' yard, ridden by Mr P W Mullins, with a 2-2-1 recent form string including a win on Good going 16 days ago — she holds every structural advantage in this race shape and is the horse all others must account for.|

runners_data.name: Searcog
runners_data.note: Patrick Magee's four-year-old has shown consistent form in similar Good-ground handicaps, most recently a second over 18f, but is a natural off-the-pace type whose redistribution to midfield means she is not racing where she is most comfortable — the style fit is marginally compromised (0.94) but her recent run is solid.|

runners_data.name: Carleys Lilly
runners_data.note: John Patrick Ryan's five-year-old has been placed at 18f on Good ground but the trainer's 14-day strike rate of 0/20 is a significant flag, and as a true hold-up type squeezed into midfield she faces the same positional difficulty as the other redistributed runners — her STYLE_FIT of 0.90 is the weakest of the trio.|

runners_data.name: Granny For Sport
runners_data.note: Lightly raced, style entirely unknown (tagged U), Ross O'Sullivan has one winner in 12 over the last fortnight — with no going record and no recent form string this runner must be treated as a complete unknown; anything she achieves here is informative rather than predictable.|

runners_data.name: Jolly D'olivate
runners_data.note: Seven-year-old with a consistent pattern of fading in finishes across three Good-ground starts at this sort of trip — 13th, 9th, 8th — and a trainer 14-day rate of 2/30 offers little encouragement that this run will differ; she is likely to be outpaced when the race quickens.|

runners_data.name: Nelliestar
runners_data.note: Thomas McGettigan's six-year-old has a single hurdles start producing a 10th on Good ground, with her wider career showing a pattern of double-figure finishes; the 7lb claimer Paddy Cleary rides, but even with that allowance there is no form evidence to suggest she can threaten in this company.|

runners_data.name: Tubberfinn Lassie
runners_data.note: Eight-year-old with a single hurdles run — seventh over 18f on Good ground — meaning she has the right going profile but nothing more to go on; style tagged unknown and trainer John Carr has one winner from seven in the last fortnight, making her a complete sit-and-watch proposition.|

runners_data.name: Moonwing
runners_data.note: Paul Gilligan's four-year-old has finished 11th in both hurdles starts on Good ground and the fade-in-finish tag is well-earned — no weight-carrying advantage and no form trajectory that suggests improvement; likely to fill the rear of the field again.|

races.paceDynamic: Cotswold Blue is the sole confirmed front-runner in this nine-runner mares maiden and, with no meaningful challenger for the lead, Willie Mullins' six-year-old under Mr P W Mullins will establish a comfortable, uncontested gallop from the front on Good ground at Sligo. The pace is unlikely to be scorching — a lone leader dictating from the front on a fair surface across 2m1½f tends to produce a measured, rhythm-based tempo that suits a horse with stamina and jumping ability rather than raw closing speed. Belladaball, Carleys Lilly, and Searcog are genuine hold-up types by profile but are all mapped to midfield because there are more off-the-pace operators in this field than the race shape can accommodate at the rear — Cotswold Blue is by far the most likely to actually secure and hold the position that suits it. This race shape strongly favours a front-runner or prominent racer who can control the tempo and jump well throughout, with Cotswold Blue holding every structural advantage in that regard.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Cotswold Blue Leads Cleanly
scenarios.trigger: If Cotswold Blue bowls along uncontested and jumps fluently, setting a steady-to-fair pace throughout.
scenarios.body: Mullins' mare controls proceedings from flag to finish on Good ground that she handles well, with no rival possessing the natural pace to press her; the race becomes a test of jumping accuracy and stamina that rewards the leader. Her form figures of 2-2-1 at this trip and going make her the standout structural fit for this shape.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Midfield Closer Pounces
scenarios.trigger: If Cotswold Blue sets a truly muddling gallop and runs out of momentum approaching the final flight.
scenarios.body: A horse tracking in mid-division conserves energy through a stop-start pace and produces a clean jump at the last to collar the tiring leader on the run-in; Belladaball, the highest-rated hold-up type with a recent win on Good ground, is the likeliest beneficiary if she can get a clean passage from her redistributed midfield berth. Her OR of 120 and proven ability at this trip give her residual claims even racing somewhat out of her preferred role.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Pace Injection Disrupts
scenarios.trigger: If one of the prominent-type redistirbuted runners — Carleys Lilly or Searcog — pushes forward early and forces Cotswold Blue to race at a faster clip than preferred.
scenarios.body: A contested gallop stretches the field and increases the premium on jumping and fitness, potentially catching Cotswold Blue out if she has not fully recovered from her run 27 days ago; the beneficiary would be a horse with recent mares form and hurdling confidence who can stay in contention throughout. Searcog's recent second on Good ground at 18f is the most relevant form reference in this shape.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Rank Outsider Surprises
scenarios.trigger: If the race deteriorates into chaos — a fall, a loose horse, or multiple errors at hurdles — and a lightly-raced unknown hits the frame.
scenarios.body: Granny For Sport or Tubberfinn Lassie, both unknown quantities on limited evidence, could steal into contention in a race that has collapsed around them; neither has the form profile to win cleanly, but a small-field mares maiden on Good ground can throw up surprises when the market leaders are compromised. Low probability but non-zero in a race with this much uncertainty at the bottom of the card.

watchPoints.text: Cotswold Blue's jumping must be monitored from the first flight — if she makes an early error she will lose her structural advantage as the sole pace-setter and the entire race shape collapses, opening the race wide.|

Belladaball is the most likely alternative winner but must secure a clean run from a midfield berth she does not naturally want — watch for her being hemmed in on the turn for home if the field concertinas.|

Carleys Lilly and Searcog could both push forward early in an attempt to get closer to their natural racing position, which would force Cotswold Blue into a more pressured gallop than her lone-leader scenario requires — monitor the first two furlongs.|

Granny For Sport is completely unexposed and Ross O'Sullivan occasionally runs lightly-raced types cold before targeting them in a race they are well-handicapped for — treat any market support with respect given the absence of any public form.|

Good ground is consistent across all seven Sligo races today with no variation reported, meaning the going read for all runners is reliable and no horse faces an unexpected surface — the pace map should play out as modelled.|

races.name: Aidan Moffitt Memorial Handicap Hurdle

runners_data.name: Fremantle Doctor
runners_data.note: Natural hold-up horse with solid Good-ground profile (three places in similar conditions), gets this trip well, but Patrick O'Brien's 5lb claim is an asset; needs clean passage in a traffic-heavy finish and has gone nine days fresh — on a going surface that suits, placed here in pattern.

runners_data.name: William F Browne
runners_data.note: The lone confirmed pace-setter; four-year-old racing prominently at a distance short of ideal (hurdle experience limited), but the uncontested lead on Good at Sligo is a genuine tactical advantage — connections have been quiet (T14: 0/22) and he has a blinker note suggesting he needs restraint.

runners_data.name: Alentejo
runners_data.note: Flagged as a finisher who fades late, which is a serious concern in a race where deep hold-up types must thread through traffic; the Good ground is fine but the fade tag and a blank recent record (890P) make this a profile with questions to answer at this distance.

runners_data.name: Tradonthebay
runners_data.note: Genuinely prominent-running type who has placed twice on Good ground and relishes distances in this range; Danny Gilligan takes the ride for in-form stable, and sitting just off William F Browne should come naturally — this is the profile the race shape most comfortably accommodates.

runners_data.name: High Honour
runners_data.note: Sixty-eight-day break is a significant concern, and the fade-in-finish flag compounds the worry; has placed on Good but the last five runs show a horse struggling for form, and P J O'Hanlon will need a big turnaround from a stale horse over a hurdle trip.

runners_data.name: Bowgate Street
runners_data.note: Has won at 18f on Good and placed four times in similar conditions — the most compelling Good-ground profile in the field; Darragh O'Keeffe is a strong booking, and the hold-up style should be manageable given the field compression means he can track closer than usual.

runners_data.name: Urban War
runners_data.note: A genuine hold-up operator by nature, pushed into a midfield position here because the field is saturated with closers — age eight with headgear (tongue-and-pads) and a run seven days ago; recent form reads 700-00 and the Good going hasn't been productive lately, limiting confidence.

runners_data.name: Tomas O Maille
runners_data.note: Nine-year-old whose true finishing style cannot be expressed cleanly in this configuration — the field's depth of hold-up types means he will be closer than ideal; Good ground is fine for him historically and Jack Gilligan's 5lb claim helps, but the form string (0-9P9P) offers little encouragement.

runners_data.name: Calm Flight Ahead
runners_data.note: Returns from an 83-day absence with a fade-in-finish flag and only one run in five that suits this going — blinkered, which may sharpen him, but the combination of a layoff, poor finishing record and weak recent form makes this a very difficult profile to trust in a competitive handicap.

runners_data.name: Invincible Oscar
runners_data.note: Off 260 days and returning from an extended break — the longest absence in the field — with a form string that includes pulled-up and unseated entries; Good ground has been manageable historically but the lengthy layoff overshadows everything, and Simon Torrens faces a stiff task on a horse that must find immediate form.

runners_data.name: Granlahan
runners_data.note: Four-year-old with a consistent placed record in Good-ground handicaps at this sort of trip — three thirds and a second in recent starts — and Daniel King rides for an Adrian McGuinness yard that has been active (T14: 5/25); naturally a hold-up horse by profile but has placed prominently enough to cope with a slightly forward position.

runners_data.name: Tasmanian Girl
runners_data.note: Has won on Good going at 17f and placed once in recent starts, so the surface and distance combination is not beyond her; Kevin Healy's 7lb claim is useful, but the form (60-P96) has been patchy and she is another natural closer who will need the pace to be strong enough to bring her into it.

runners_data.name: Wings Of Africa
runners_data.note: Fades in the finish and has not won in recent starts, with a form string including pulled-up; the Going is acceptable but the fade flag and lack of winning form combine with a 12-day turnaround to leave this horse needing significant improvement — Ben Kennedy's claim is the main positive.

races.paceDynamic: William F Browne is the sole confirmed front-runner in this 13-runner handicap hurdle at Sligo, and with no genuine rival pressing him for the lead, he is set to control the tempo from the front at a sustainable, unhurried gallop on Good ground. Behind him, the field is overwhelmingly populated by hold-up types — Fremantle Doctor, Bowgate Street, Tradonthebay, Granlahan and others — who will settle in behind and wait for the race to develop from the middle stages. The compressed nature of the field in the chasing pack means the straight at Sligo will see a mass of closers launching simultaneously, creating a scenario where only those with clean passage and a genuine late kick will be rewarded. This race shape — a controlled single pace-setter and a wall of finishers — decisively favours prominent trackers who can sit just off William F Browne without covering too much ground, rather than deep hold-up horses who must weave through traffic; the field holds significantly more hold-up types than can realistically obtain their preferred rear position, with Urban War, Tomas O Maille, Granlahan, Calm Flight Ahead and Invincible Oscar all likely to be pushed forward from their natural stations, meaning Tradonthebay and Bowgate Street — legitimate prominent/tracking profiles — are best placed to capitalise on the race shape.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Controlled Pace, Tracker Wins
scenarios.trigger: If William F Browne sets a measured gallop and prominent trackers like Tradonthebay and Bowgate Street travel comfortably just behind throughout.
scenarios.body: William F Browne softens the field with a fair pace and the well-positioned trackers pounce turning for home, leaving the deeper hold-up horses with too much ground to make up on Good going at Sligo.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Front-Runner Lasts Home
scenarios.trigger: If William F Browne exploits his uncontested lead and the rest fail to close the gap efficiently through the cramped Sligo straight.
scenarios.body: Racing unchallenged, William F Browne conserves energy and kicks again at the second-last, with the chasing pack failing to coordinate a clean run at him.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Late Closers Pounce
scenarios.trigger: If the pace set by William F Browne proves genuinely fast enough to string out the field and create a closing opportunity for deeper hold-up horses.
scenarios.body: Fremantle Doctor or Granlahan, producing a strong late run from off the pace, benefit if traffic clears early enough in the straight at Sligo.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Pace Collapse, Outsider Wins
scenarios.trigger: If a false tempo or a melee in the chasing pack causes traffic carnage and an unconsidered runner emerges from the chaos.
scenarios.body: The lack of genuine strong pace creates a sprint finish in which lower-weighted runners with fresh legs and good position benefit disproportionately.

watchPoints.text: Tradonthebay — if Danny Gilligan slots him just behind William F Browne in the first two, this horse's prominent profile is perfectly matched to the race shape and he could prove hard to peg back turning for home.

Bowgate Street — Darragh O'Keeffe is too good a judge to let the traffic situation derail a horse with a 14/15 record on Good going and a course-distance win; watch for him to manoeuvre into the ideal inside line early.

William F Browne — monitor whether Josh Williamson allows him to dictate or pushes on enough to test the closers; if he idles in front on a sustainable tempo, the trackers will have a straightforward task, but if he quickens from three out, his stamina at 4yo over this trip becomes a factor.

Traffic trouble in the straight — with 13 runners, the majority of whom are hold-up types forced into midfield, the Sligo straight is likely to become congested; watch for Fremantle Doctor and Granlahan to be caught in traffic if they cannot find a clear run before the second-last.

Invincible Oscar — 260 days off is the standout layoff flag in this field; if he shows any unusual early market support it may suggest a stable confidence angle worth monitoring, but on published form the absence alone warrants caution.

races.name: Solar Generation Maiden Hurdle

runners_data.name: Godsend
runners_data.note: Hold-up operator with genuine winning form over this trip on Good ground (three wins at 14-17f on Good), but his OR-120 and 18-day return look fine — the concern is whether a controlled Mindyourheadmike pace generates enough pace for him to pick up late; Cian Collins yard shows 0/13 at 14-day runner rate, limiting confidence from a training angle.

runners_data.name: Mindyourheadmike
runners_data.note: The race-shaper: sole confirmed front-runner who won at 16f on Good and has recent course form; claiming rider Finegan takes 5lb, trainer Ciaran Murphy 3/12 in 14 days, and with no pace rival he can dictate entirely — this horse is the structural key to the whole race.

runners_data.name: Discrete
runners_data.note: Held-up horse who ran just 9 days ago and has shown 0 wins from 2 starts on similar going; tongue-tie applied and form string (FP-607) is uninspiring, making this a speculative hold-up play that needs the pace to be honest to get competitive.

runners_data.name: Go To The Moon
runners_data.note: Prominent-style runner whose best form includes a win, though his two similar-going runs produced 7th and 12th; the 44-day break is not alarming but the modest recent record and lightly-winning trainer rate (0/6 in 14 days) temper expectations.

runners_data.name: Lengaruka
runners_data.note: Lightly raced and flagged as a notable unknown — only two hurdle runs on record (5th and 10th), going profile shows OK but no wins or places; the unexposed angle is the only real interest and John Shinnick rides for a stable with minimal recent volume.

runners_data.name: Seven Towers
runners_data.note: Keith Donoghue partners a horse with four placed runs from five hurdle starts, all at roughly this trip on similar ground — the most consistently performed horse in the field behind the leader; Cromwell's 4/14 in 14 days gives the yard some recent form, and a prominent style makes him the natural alternative if Mindyourheadmike stops.

runners_data.name: Hadahi
runners_data.note: Four-year-old returning after 94 days with going experience unconfirmed (flagged UNKNOWN) and lightly-raced status; form includes an unseated runner and mixed finishes, making him genuinely difficult to assess — Simon Torrens rides and Kelly's yard 1/8 in 14 days offers modest support.

runners_data.name: Kisuton Enki
runners_data.note: Jack Kennedy's booking for Gordon Elliott (4/38 in 14 days, active yard) is the most eye-catching jockey-trainer angle in the race; prominent style with placed form at 18f on Good and softer, but 84 days off and a rating that has not translated into wins (0 wins from recent runs) means he needs to reproduce his better efforts fresh.

races.paceDynamic: Mindyourheadmike is the sole confirmed front-runner in this 8-runner maiden hurdle and, with no credible pace rival to pressurise him, Eoghan Finegan (claiming 5lb) should be able to dictate a controlled, measured gallop over the 2m4½f trip on Good ground at Sligo. Seven Towers and Go To The Moon are prominent-stylied horses that will track but neither profiles as a true pace-pusher, so the leader is likely to set a rhythm entirely on his own terms. Behind him, the hold-up brigade — Godsend and Discrete — will be waiting for a run that may come too late if the pace is genuinely sustainable and the race never truly stretches. The race shape strongly favours a front-running or close-tracking prominent profile: a controlled pace with a single leader allows that leader and the horses immediately behind him to conserve energy and sprint clear, penalising horses reliant on a stronger gallop to generate a winning run.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Leader Controls, Wins
scenarios.trigger: If Mindyourheadmike bowls along uncontested and the pace remains measured throughout.
scenarios.body: Finegan settles the horse into a comfortable rhythm with no pressure from behind, ensuring the leader hits the final bend full of running and has enough left to kick clear on the run-in; Good ground at Sligo on a tight circuit suits a front-runner who doesn't need to be spectacular over hurdles, just efficient.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Prominent Tracker Pounces
scenarios.trigger: If Mindyourheadmike weakens late and a prominent chaser swoops in the final 2f.
scenarios.body: Seven Towers has placed four times in five hurdle starts at this trip and going, and his consistency from a prominent position makes him the most logical beneficiary if the leader fails to sustain; Kisuton Enki, reunited with Jack Kennedy and returning fresh, also has the close-tracking profile to capitalise on any late error or fade from the leader.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Closers Land Late
scenarios.trigger: If the early gallop is deceptively strong and the field strings out, opening a late lane for hold-up horses.
scenarios.body: Godsend has winning form at this trip on Good ground and a hold-up style that could see him finish powerfully if the pace genuinely collapses those in front; Discrete is similarly held-up but his recent form and maiden-going flag make him a riskier proposition in this scenario.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Chaos/Outsider Lands Blow
scenarios.trigger: If multiple fallers, evasions or market leaders underperform and the race becomes ragged.
scenarios.body: Hadahi is an unknown quantity returning after 94 days with lightly-raced status and going experience unconfirmed; Lengaruka is similarly unexposed and could outrun market expectations if the race unravels in front of him.

watchPoints.text: Mindyourheadmike is the fulcrum of the entire race — if he jumps poorly at any of the early hurdles or Finegan struggles to find a rhythm in his first real race-riding opportunity here, the entire anticipated pace dynamic collapses and the race becomes chaotic.

Seven Towers has been off 47 days and faces his most competitive test, but his pattern of four placings without a win raises the question of whether he can convert — watch to see if Donoghue positions him within striking distance or allows a gap to open.

Kisuton Enki is 84 days fresh for Gordon Elliott with Jack Kennedy aboard — the booking alone makes him one to monitor in the market; if he drifts significantly pre-race, that 84-day layoff and soft-ground form pattern may be telling.

Godsend's hold-up style in a race likely to be run at a controlled pace is a tactical mismatch — watch how Gilligan positions him early; if he is forced to race closer than usual, his winning form at the trip becomes more relevant, but if he settles last, the moderate pace may leave him too much to do.

races.name: McDermott Farm Machinery Handicap Hurdle

runners_data.name: Wild Mandate
runners_data.note: The lone confirmed front-runner at OR 96; Good-ground form reads 14 starts for 1 win and 6 places, she is at home on this surface, and with the hood and tongue-tie fitted she is set to control the race from the front — the [STYLE_FIT] flag signals she is racing slightly out of her usual role but she is clearly the pace anchor here.

runners_data.name: Laska Du Breuil
runners_data.note: Gavin Cromwell's five-year-old returns off an 83-day break having won last time out on Soft — the switch to Good is a query, but her 22f win came on Soft and her handicap mark of OR 94 makes her competitive if coming fit; Keith Donoghue is a strong booking and her hold-up style suits a big-field scenario where late finishers can exploit a steady pace.

runners_data.name: Phoenix Arizona
runners_data.note: Consistent hold-up performer who has placed four times from 11 runs on Good ground at around this distance; the 7lb claimer O'Connor is a small negative, but the horse's form figures of 2-3-4 at this trip on this going make her a reliable each-way profile regardless of how the race is run.

runners_data.name: Georginas Jet
runners_data.note: Five-year-old hold-up mare who won at 18f on Good ground and has placed regularly; the 5lb claim from Gilligan helps at the weights, and her yard sends her here in good enough recent form — she is the type who will benefit if others in front of her tire late.

runners_data.name: Love Like This
runners_data.note: Versatile hold-up operator at OR 88 who won at 24f on Good last time and has placed at 23-25f, suggesting this 20f trip suits; the 7lb claimer Barry slightly dilutes confidence but the mare's consistency on Good ground over staying trips makes her a genuine player in any scenario where the pace is controlled.

runners_data.name: Ranting And Raven
runners_data.note: Gavin Cromwell's four-year-old has been running out of form of late (form string 60-697) and all five recent runs on Good ground have returned finishing positions of 6 to 10 — pace pattern here will not help a hold-up type who has struggled to produce any late effort.

runners_data.name: Beacon Bypass
runners_data.note: Runs out of petrol late (⚠ fades in finish tag) and all four recent runs on Good have ended outside the first eight — in truth a genuine hold-up horse whose midfield mapping is a redistribution artefact given this crowded field, and the overall profile does not inspire at OR 86.

runners_data.name: Sekakarma
runners_data.note: Nine-year-old veteran whose natural tendency is to race from the rear, mapped here to midfield purely because the hold-up ranks are overcrowded — his best recent effort was a second at 20f on Good and the trip should suit, but he has not won in some time and OR 82 is a tough ask.

runners_data.name: Katie's Casper
runners_data.note: Has placed twice at 24f on Good ground and showed a 2nd at that trip, so the distance is fine; however the hold-up style is squeezed into a midfield slot by field logistics rather than genuine positioning, and the trainer's 1/7 recent strike rate over 14 days is a mild positive without being convincing.

runners_data.name: Mother Ship
runners_data.note: Consistent hold-up performer who has placed three times at 20-22f on Good ground, but recent form shows 5-8-8-0-7 and she has not threatened to win in this company — naturally a rear-running type forced into a midfield slot by the volume of closers in this field, making her tactical position even less favourable.

runners_data.name: Gortmore Lady
runners_data.note: Six-year-old whose three recent placing runs came at 18-22f on Good ground; the trainer Ciaran Murphy sends her here having had 3 winners from 12 over 14 days which is a positive angle, but her redistribution from true hold-up to midfield means she will not find her natural rhythm, and the tendency to finish around 7th-9th is a concern.

runners_data.name: Clever Court
runners_data.note: Won at 20f on Good ground from hold-up tactics and has placed once — the most interesting of the redistributed closers because that win shows real ability at this trip and on this surface; Shane O'Callaghan (3lb claimer) is a useful booking, and if he can navigate from a midfield slot in a big field there is more here than the OR 77 suggests.

runners_data.name: El Arco
runners_data.note: Gordon Elliott-trained five-year-old returning from a 146-day layoff — the extended absence is the headline concern, and all seven runs on Good have produced a best of 5th; mapped to midfield rather than his natural hold-up position, the lack of match fitness means he is best watched on debut back.

runners_data.name: Move It On Over
runners_data.note: Carries the ⚠ fades in finish flag and has finished in the first four only once across nine runs on Good ground — a genuine closer by nature but one who has not demonstrated the finishing kick required when the race is run at a moderate tempo set by Wild Mandate.

runners_data.name: Glaoinn An Airgead
runners_data.note: Eight-year-old with a form string of F0-0P0 and 14 runs on Good ground returning finishes of 10th-12th — the fade flag is apt and there is little in the evidence to suggest this run will differ, even if the midfield slot is simply a redistribution of his true rear-running style.

runners_data.name: Max Time
runners_data.note: Prominent-style runner at OR 72 who fades in finishes — the only horse likely to attend Wild Mandate in the early stages, but his tendency to weaken late and a recent run of PP04P makes him a danger only in terms of unsettling the early pace, not in terms of being a realistic winner.

runners_data.name: Hob's Angel
runners_data.note: Ten-year-old whose form shows wins at 20f on Good ground and places at 24f — genuine claims on form at this distance, and Barcoe's yard has been quiet recently but the horse's record of 1W and 3P on Good is respectable; as a natural hold-up type mapped to midfield, he is slightly disadvantaged positionally but the stamina profile is solid.

runners_data.name: Firstupbestdressed
runners_data.note: The fade flag and form of UU4-30 with 14 runs on Good producing a best of 6th tells a clear story — a six-year-old whose hold-up style is genuine but whose finishing effort has consistently disappointed, and being mapped to midfield does not change the underlying form concern.

races.paceDynamic: Wild Mandate is the sole confirmed front-runner in this 18-runner handicap hurdle over 2m4½f at Sligo, and with no genuine pace rival to push her, she is set to control proceedings at a measured, sustainable gallop on Good ground. Max Time has prominent tendencies and may attempt to sit close, but is prone to fading and poses no real threat to Wild Mandate's command of the early tempo. The vast majority of this field are natural hold-up horses — Laska Du Breuil, Phoenix Arizona, Georginas Jet, Love Like This, Ranting And Raven, Mother Ship, and many others — but with so many closers crowding the rear, those mapped to midfield (Beacon Bypass, Sekakarma, Katie's Casper, Gortmore Lady, Clever Court, El Arco, and others) are operating out of their natural position and cannot all secure the ground they prefer. A single front-runner dictating an uncontested rhythm over this stamina trip on Good ground strongly favours resolute hold-up performers with proven form at 2m4f or beyond who can produce a sustained finish rather than a sharp late burst, with those sitting closest to the pace in the first half of the race best positioned to strike.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Wild Mandate Controls Unchallenged
scenarios.trigger: If Wild Mandate is allowed to stride along in front without any rival forcing a genuinely searching gallop, setting a measured pace that suits her stamina.
scenarios.body: Wild Mandate dictates every yard from flag to finish on her favoured Good ground, drawing on her prominent racing style and experience, and the tempo is simply not strong enough to bring the mass of closers into play late.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Hold-Up Horses Sweep Late
scenarios.trigger: If the pace is just brisk enough to stretch the field and allow genuine closers who secure a clear run to reel in the leader in the final half-mile.
scenarios.body: With 18 runners, traffic problems are real, but horses like Laska Du Breuil and Georginas Jet — both with strong Good-ground form at this sort of trip — have the class and patience to pick through and benefit from any late fade at the front.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Prominent Stalker Pounces
scenarios.trigger: If a horse sitting just off Wild Mandate in second or third makes a smooth move turning for home and outstays everything else.
scenarios.body: Love Like This has form at 2m4f on Good ground and knows how to win from off the pace at a reasonable gallop; Phoenix Arizona has placed consistently at around this trip and could track the pace closely enough to strike.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Chaos And Attrition
scenarios.trigger: If the large field causes early crowding, jumping errors cause fallers, and the race breaks apart into a ragged contest where a resolute stayer grinds it out.
scenarios.body: With 18 runners over hurdles at a sharp, tight track like Sligo, bunching at the early flights is a real possibility; Hob's Angel, who has won off this sort of mark and handles Good ground well, could emerge from the carnage, as could Clever Court who landed a recent win at this trip.

watchPoints.text: Wild Mandate is the only horse setting the pace in an 18-runner field — if she gets a clean lead unchallenged, watch whether Max Time or any other horse attempts to press her, as that could be the only scenario that changes the tempo and opens the race up.

With 18 runners jumping hurdles at Sligo's tight, sharp track, the risk of crowding and early jumping incidents is elevated — horses in the middle of the pack (Beacon Bypass, Sekakarma, Gortmore Lady) will need a clean passage that may simply not materialise.

Several redistributed hold-up horses (Beacon Bypass, Sekakarma, Katie's Casper, Mother Ship, Clever Court) are all tagged [STYLE_FIT] with scores of 0.90-0.93, meaning none of them are in their preferred race position — watch whether any of them manage to drop back to their natural ground before the first flight.

Laska Du Breuil returns off 83 days for Gavin Cromwell who also runs Ranting And Raven — watch her at the start and over the early flights for any signs of freshness or ring-rustiness that might compromise her hold-up run.

Love Like This and Georginas Jet are both on short turnarounds of 15 and 13 days respectively — both were placed or won last time, and how sharp they look in the early stages will indicate whether either is primed for a challenge late over this stamina trip.

races.name: Francie 'Banger' Burns Handicap Hurdle

runners_data.name: In For The Night
runners_data.note: Strong form on Good ground (3 wins/5 places from 12 similar-ground runs) and a recent placed effort 26 days ago; held-up style means he needs the pace to be genuinely strong, and at 166lbs he carries a significant weight burden for this trip.

runners_data.name: In The Minus
runners_data.note: Won last time out 13 days ago and trainer Cawley has a 1/1 form line in the 14-day window; a hold-up operator who has shown he can finish well on Good, but the weight of natural closers in this field makes getting a clear run from the rear a tactical challenge.

runners_data.name: Drombane
runners_data.note: Mullins-trained, and the yard's 14-day strike rate of 12/27 adds confidence; has placed twice over 2m4f on Good, races prominently which suits this shape, and the headgear (tongue-tie) is retained — he is one of the better-placed prominent types to profit from tracking Crystabel.

runners_data.name: Harpy Eagle
runners_data.note: Won last time out on Good ground over 2m4f 11 days ago, races prominently and the 7lb claimer Cody partners a horse in fine form; the concern is whether an OR of 105 and 157lbs is enough of a platform to sustain the effort up the Sligo straight.

runners_data.name: Tangara Bay
runners_data.note: A hold-up horse that won on Soft and has struggled on Good (0W0P in 2 similar-going runs); Peter Fahey's runner finds this surface less forgiving and the further ground needed to weave through from the rear adds risk.

runners_data.name: Bossy Bird
runners_data.note: Placed second on Good ground over 2m4f and shows ability, but his natural hold-up style means he is effectively racing outside his comfort zone today — the overcrowded rear means he sits in midfield rather than where he would choose, tempering expectations accordingly.

runners_data.name: Crystabel
runners_data.note: The lone front-runner with 10 runs on Good (1W5P) and a clear course-and-distance profile over 2m2f-2m4f; at 154lbs and with Daniel King riding for a stable sending out 20 runners in 14 days with no winners, the question is stamina and market confidence rather than ability to lead.

runners_data.name: Coolboy Christy
runners_data.note: A genuine hold-up type by profile who gets nudged into midfield by the congestion at the rear; his best form (4/24f Good) suggests the trip is fine, but the headgear (prickers) is new and the stable's modest 14-day record (2/30) tempers enthusiasm.

runners_data.name: Midnight Eagle
runners_data.note: Flagged as a horse that fades in the finish — a significant concern over 2m4½f; his true hold-up style is compromised by being pushed to midfield, and three recent top-three finishes over shorter trips (2m1f) suggest this distance may be at the outer edge of his stamina.

runners_data.name: Ladiam
runners_data.note: Nine-year-old who races prominently and has a 14/15 record on similar going (1W7P), so the surface holds no fears; the 9-day turnaround is quick and OR 92 is competitive in this grade, with the tongue-tie retained — he is an honest stayer who suits the expected shape.

runners_data.name: Dream Shaper
runners_data.note: Won on Good over 2m3f and the tongue-tie is noted; 7lb claimer Halford takes the ride for a stable without recent winners (0/3 in 14 days), and the prominent style is a positive in this pace map — the fall on record adds a small jumping integrity query.

races.paceDynamic: Crystabel is the sole confirmed front-runner and, with no genuine rival likely to push her from the outset, she should be able to control the tempo on her own terms over this 2m4½f trip at Sligo — a track that rewards settled, fluent jumpers rather than hard-held closers. The pacemaker's ability to dictate a sustainable gallop on Good ground means the race will likely be run at an even, honest clip without a brutal early injection of pace, keeping the field compact through the middle stages and denying true sit-and-deliver hold-up horses a meaningful advantage at the finish. Drombane, Harpy Eagle, Ladiam, and Dream Shaper are the genuine prominent types and represent the main pressers in behind, though Bossy Bird, Midnight Eagle, and Coolboy Christy — all natural hold-up types — are mapped into midfield positions because the field contains more rear-rank horses than the topology can accommodate, meaning at least some of them will not secure their preferred ground. This race shape overwhelmingly favours horses that race prominently or just off the pace, able to track Crystabel, pounce at the second-last, and see out the distance cleanly on a surface that rewards accuracy and stamina rather than a late finishing burst.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Crystabel Controls, Prominent Win
scenarios.trigger: If Crystabel sets a measured, uncontested gallop and prominent horses track her into the straight.
scenarios.body: Crystabel leads throughout at a sensible pace on Good ground, and the horses sitting second or third in the travelling order are best placed to hit the front two out and consolidate; the steady fractions suit those with clean jumping and stamina rather than a turn of foot.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Pace Quickens, Stayers Arrive
scenarios.trigger: If the pace picks up sharply from halfway and the run from the rear becomes viable for genuine hold-up types.
scenarios.body: A stronger gallop set by Crystabel with Drombane or Ladiam pressing stretches the field and opens a gap for a well-timed late run; In For The Night or In The Minus, both having won over Good ground, are best credentialed to close if the pace is truly unrelenting.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Crystabel Wins Unchallenged
scenarios.trigger: If the field is slow to challenge and Crystabel is allowed to stride clear in the straight uncontested.
scenarios.body: With a light weight, Good ground she handles well and a jockey who lets her stride, Crystabel simply refuses to be pegged back and the prominent horses behind lack the firepower to reel her in; her 1W5P record on Good ground underlines she can see it out.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Held-Up Types Profit Late
scenarios.trigger: If the gallop is surprisingly strong enough from the outset that the redistributed hold-up horses can close meaningfully despite racing out of their ideal role.
scenarios.body: This scenario depends on Bossy Bird, Midnight Eagle, or Coolboy Christy — all displaced from their natural rear berth — finding a clear run and producing a finishing effort, which is materially less likely given the modest pace projection and their compromised position; it cannot be ruled out entirely but the style-fit penalties and lack of a truly searching tempo make it a low-probability outcome.

watchPoints.text: Crystabel's lead could go entirely unchallenged — watch whether any of the prominent horses (Drombane, Harpy Eagle) press her from the outset, as a fully uncontested front-runner on Good ground at Sligo is a materially different proposition to one who has to fight for her position.

Midnight Eagle is flagged as a horse who fades in the finish and is already racing outside his natural hold-up role; if he gets outpaced jumping the second-last, he could cause interference in a tightly grouped field.

Bossy Bird and Coolboy Christy are both true hold-up horses crammed into midfield — watch the early stages for crowding and shuffling between these two as riders look for room that may not exist in an 11-runner field.

The 7lb claimer trio (Paddy Cody on Harpy Eagle, Harry Sexton on Bossy Bird, Conor Clarke on Coolboy Christy) all ride in the same race; positional errors from inexperienced riders in the midfield cluster could alter the shape of the race from the third-last hurdle.

Drombane's Mullins yard is firing at 12/27 in the 14-day window — watch for any market move at the off, as a well-supported Mullins prominent racer with proven staying form on Good is the type that can take advantage of a controlled pace set by Crystabel.

races.name: Adare Manor Opportunity Handicap Hurdle

runners_data.name: Ringdufferin
runners_data.note: Genuine hold-up horse for A L T Moore with Calum Hogan claiming 2lbs; 10 from 15 runs on Good ground with two places from five comparable runs, making him a clean fit for this going, and at 36 days fresh he arrives in good order — the natural closing role in a race with a contested pace suits him well.

runners_data.name: Luck Between Us
runners_data.note: Won last time out over 20f on Good ground 34 days ago for Donncha Duggan, boosting his record to 1W3P from 5 Good-ground runs, and the step up to 3m1½f is unexplored territory — if the stamina holds, his style of closing from off the pace is ideally aligned with the expected race shape.

runners_data.name: Dorans Law
runners_data.note: Ran just nine days ago and has been kept very busy by P J Rothwell; his record of 13 from 15 runs on Good ground is outstanding (1W5P), and the tongue-strap is noted, but despite a natural hold-up style he will need traffic to part for him late given how many others are also operating from the same rear position.

runners_data.name: Cornmarket
runners_data.note: Prominent racer for John J Cullen who gets a 4lb claim from Alan King; his second over 26f on Good ground is the stand-out piece of form here and he is the most natural tracker of the pace in this field — the blinkered headgear sharpens his jumping focus and his fitness (13 days) is fine.

runners_data.name: Keep Em Quite
runners_data.note: Confirmed front-runner for Cian Collins with an apprentice claim; has run twice in nine days which raises mild fitness questions but his Good-ground second over 22f is recent evidence of ability at this trip — he must lead to be effective and will have a battle with Tango Theatre early on.

runners_data.name: Ilbdare
runners_data.note: Won over 26f on Good ground for Mark McNiff and returns after 71 days off with a tongue-strap; instinctively a hold-up horse by nature, this crowded rear section means he is likely to find himself further forward than preferred, which tempers confidence despite the strong course-trip profile.

runners_data.name: Mr Dibbs
runners_data.note: Gavin Cromwell's runner carries the blinkered headgear and boasts a win over 26f on Good ground among his recent runs (2W4P from 11 Good-ground starts); ran 15 days ago and a prominent-to-midfield position suits — he is one of the more interesting holding horses who actually has scope to race nearer the pace than the map suggests.

runners_data.name: Sallap
runners_data.note: Has two wins on Good ground over 22f but is flagged as a horse that fades in the finish — a concern at 3m1½f on a stamina track; his natural hold-up position is squeezed by the volume of closers in this field, and with a tongue-strap fitted, his ability to even get his preferred spot is in doubt, making the finishing fade warning particularly relevant here.

runners_data.name: Tango Theatre
runners_data.note: Veteran 11-year-old who wears a tongue-strap and a visor and habitually leads; has solid Good-ground form (1W5P from 11 runs) and ran 12 days ago, but at this age and in a two-way speed duel with Keep Em Quite over 3m1½f, the concern is that he burns up before the straight and weakens out of contention — his role is as a pace-generator rather than a winner.

runners_data.name: Hey Babbs
runners_data.note: Returned 123 days ago after a lengthy break for Dermot McLoughlin; at 6 years old with a hold-up style, the extended absence and the congested closing ground mean he carries significant risk — Good ground form exists (1W4P) but the fitness question off that long layoff is the overriding concern today.

runners_data.name: The Little Yank
runners_data.note: An 11-year-old for John Patrick Ryan who has placed twice in his last two runs over 25f on Good ground with a claiming jockey; his Good-ground record is modest (0W3P from 6 runs) and at this age in a competitive handicap with a busy rear section, finding a clear run late enough to matter will be very difficult.

runners_data.name: Strong Contender
runners_data.note: Youngest in the field at 5, won last time over 24f on Good ground 12 days ago for Norman Lee, and his Good-ground record is 1W2P from 6 runs — the most relevant positive; however, he is naturally a hold-up horse operating in a congested closing group, and the step up in class and the positional squeeze both represent real obstacles to following up.

races.paceDynamic: Keep Em Quite and Tango Theatre are the two confirmed front-runners here and both are likely to press on from the off over this 3m1½f trip at Sligo, creating a genuine, honest gallop rather than a falsely-run affair. Keep Em Quite has been competing at shorter trips recently and will be keen to get to the front, while the veteran Tango Theatre (11yo) habitually leads and will not concede that role easily, meaning a contested pace is the base expectation. This sustained early pressure over a stiff three-mile-plus trip on Good ground will stretch the field out and tend to favour horses who can travel with cover and finish strongly in the home straight — a profile that suits the genuine prominent/midfield runners rather than those who need to make ground from the very back. The field contains considerably more hold-up types than the race shape can accommodate at the rear: Ilbdare, Sallap, Hey Babbs, The Little Yank and Strong Contender are all true hold-up horses redistributed forward on the map, meaning Ringdufferin, Luck Between Us and Dorans Law — the runners who can genuinely race in that tactical space — have the clearest positional advantage under an honest gallop.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Contested Pace, Closers Reign
scenarios.trigger: If Keep Em Quite and Tango Theatre fight for the lead and set a genuine honest gallop throughout, draining their own reserves.
scenarios.body: The two front-runners burn each other up over this demanding trip, leaving those who have tracked in cover from midfield with a decisive advantage in the straight; the stiff Sligo finish on Good ground rewards those with a clean jumper's rhythm and stamina to pick up. Horses with genuine hold-up credentials who can get their natural position thrive here, particularly those with solid Good-ground records at staying trips.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Front-Runner Dominates Unchallenged
scenarios.trigger: If Tango Theatre drops away early or fails to contest the lead, leaving Keep Em Quite to bowl along at a controlled, uncontested tempo.
scenarios.body: Keep Em Quite is freed from early pressure and is permitted to dictate a measured gallop, conserving enough to fight back when challenged from the second-last; a solo leader at a sustainable pace on Good ground at Sligo can be very hard to reel in over this trip. Prominent types who track close to the leader are better placed than true closers in this shape, and Keep Em Quite's recent second over 22f on Good ground is a direct pointer.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Prominent Stalkers Pounce
scenarios.trigger: If the front two set a strong pace and a prominent-to-midfield horse improves smoothly off their heels to lead at the last.
scenarios.body: A horse like Cornmarket or Mr Dibbs, able to race in third or fourth throughout and avoid the early scrimmage, would be ideally positioned to challenge when the front-runners weaken; this shape rewards clean jumping and a good cruising speed rather than finishing speed alone. Cornmarket's second over 26f on Good ground and Mr Dibbs' win at the same trip on Good are both directly relevant to this scenario.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Chaos Late Run Succeeds
scenarios.trigger: If multiple fences go wrong early, the pace collapses or fallers disrupt the race, gifting a late-closing run from the back.
scenarios.body: This scenario requires the natural hold-up horses — several of whom are mapped out of their true position — to get back to their preferred spot and deliver a late charge, which is the least likely shape given how many genuine closers are competing for the same ground. Sallap and Strong Contender have the finishing profile but their positional constraints and style-fit discounts make this a low-probability outcome.

watchPoints.text: Keep Em Quite and Tango Theatre are both confirmed front-runners — watch the first two furlongs to see if either blinks and concedes the lead, because whoever gets their nose in front unchallenged changes this from a truly-run race to a falsely-run one and dramatically lifts the winner's chance.

Sallap is flagged as a horse that fades in the finish and is also redistributed out of his natural hold-up position — if he is forced wider or further forward than ideal in the early stages, his tendency to weaken late becomes an even greater liability at this trip.

Hey Babbs returns after 123 days off and is one of five genuine hold-up horses competing for the same closing ground — watch in the first mile to see whether he settles comfortably or travels laboured, as fitness after that layoff will be exposed quickly on a stiff track like Sligo.

Luck Between Us tackles 3m1½f for the first time having won over 20f last time — watch how he travels into the final bend, as the stamina question only gets answered in the final quarter-mile and if he is still travelling well jumping the second-last his chance is live.

Cornmarket is the one prominent-style horse in a field dominated by closers and front-runners — if he slots into third or fourth early and travels without being asked a question, he becomes the key dangers horse for the closers to beat, so his jumping and position through the first circuit is worth monitoring closely.
